title: Streaming Function Orbit: orchestrated function/tool resolution with loop-safety
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: multi-tool/function call loops can create unbounded recursion, deadlocks, and ambiguous structured output when combined with streaming responses and compatibility fallbacks for older tool implementations. Current behavior: streaming tokens are emitted interleaved with tool metadata; legacy tools return free-form text as the final token which breaks structured output parsing. Goal: implement an execution loop that supports chained function/tool calls, preserves streaming semantics, enforces loop/recursion guards, and provides a backward-compatible compatibility layer so older tool adapters can opt into the structured-output contract without immediate rewrites.
non_goals: This ticket does not implement a new authoritative tool schema registry (separate project). It does not change pricing or Dedicated scaling policies. Deep model-level kernel scheduling improvements are out of scope.
proposal_summary: Introduce a lightweight orchestration layer in the request executor that: 1) wraps each tool invocation with a deterministic envelope (id, variant, tokenized-stream-marker), 2) maintains a per-request call graph and depth counter with TTL and global per-request budget, 3) supports progressive streaming of structured envelopes (partial=true/false) so consumers can safely parse incomplete outputs, and 4) provides a compatibility shim that wraps legacy tool responses into the structured envelope with best-effort extraction heuristics and confidence metadata.
technical_design: Execution model: executor runs as a state machine with phases: INITIAL -> INVOKE_TOOL -> STREAM_PART -> INJECT_RESULT -> PROCESS_RESULT -> DECIDE_NEXT (INVOKE_TOOL | RETURN | FAIL). Each tool invocation gets an idempotency token and a monotonic call-depth counter. Loop detection: maintain a small LRU of tool-call fingerprints (tool_id + normalized_input_hash). If fingerprint repeats beyond threshold (configurable, default 3) within the same request, mark as potential loop and trigger a soft-fail policy (try alternate tool variant or return a concise structured error). Deadlock avoidance: tool invocations that require additional streaming input must advertise 'needs_more_input' flag; the orchestrator enforces a max-wait timer (default 500ms) and will fallback to stubbed response or error if unmet.
structured_streaming_contract: All streaming payloads are JSON lines where each line is an envelope with fields: envelope_id, phase, payload_type (text|json|tool_meta), partial (true|false), provenance (list of tool ids or 'model'), and optional confidence. Consumer parsing: consumers must buffer until partial==false for final assembly. Backward compatibility: compatibility shim emits these envelopes even when the underlying tool returns legacy text by wrapping text in payload_type=text and including heuristic-extracted JSON in payload_type=json with confidence <0.7.
compatibility_layer:
Adapters implement a simple interface: adapt(v1_response) -> structured_envelopes[]. A set of heuristics (JSON-first, yaml-block, key-value pairs) is used to identify embedded structured content. Adapters can register 'compatibility hints' which declare common patterns. We provide reference adapters for:
- legacy-python-tool v0.9
- webhook-based tools
- third-party search-as-a-tool
acceptance_criteria: 1) Executor returns structured JSON-line envelopes for chained tool calls in streaming mode; 2) Loop guard prevents repeated fingerprint >3 and triggers fallbacks in reproducible test; 3) Compatibility shim successfully wraps 90% of sampled legacy tool responses into structured envelopes (measured by heuristic tests); 4) End-to-end latency regression <5% on 95th percentile for standard small tool chains; 5) Unit + integration tests and a docs PR merged.
test_plan: Unit tests for state machine transitions, loop fingerprinting, and TTL expiry. Integration tests with: - mock legacy tool that returns raw text and a version that returns structured JSON; - streaming client that assembles envelopes and verifies partial->final semantics; - stress test that simulates recursive tool calls to validate circuit-breaker behavior. Add e2e scenario in QA pipeline with trace-level logging enabled.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated rollout: opt-in via request header X-Run-Orbit=alpha. Stage 1: internal smoke tests with alpha flag. Stage 2: invite-only customers and infra partners. Stage 3: gradual percentage rollout with metrics dashboard (loop-detections, compatibility-unwrap-rate, consumer-parse-errors). Provide fallback default behavior (pre-flag) identical to current production for safety.
migration_and_compatibility: Provide shim library in SDKs (python/js) versioned as orbit-shim v0.1. SDKs can be used server-side or by customers to wrap tool implementations. Document common migration patterns and an automated linter that flags tools not emitting envelopes. Plan 3-month deprecation notice for older adapters after orbit-shim reaches v1.0 and adoption metrics exceed threshold.
observability_and_metrics: Emit metrics: orbit.loop_detected (counter, labels: request_origin, tool_family), envelope.emitted (counter), envelope.partial_rate (gauge), compatibility.unwrap_rate (ratio), orbit.fallback_triggered. Trace spans: executor.call, adapter.wrap, injector.merge. Dashboard: new card in Console under runtime-2.4 -> Orchestration -> Orbit.
security_considerations: Structured envelopes may expose tool provenance and intermediate results. Default retention for intermediate envelopes = 24h; configurable per-customer. Ensure compatibility adapter sanitizes secrets and PII with the existing redaction library. Security review required before enabling globally.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Use fingerprint-based loop detection (fast, small memory) vs full call-graph cycle detection (more accurate but heavier). Chosen fingerprint for 95% of cases.
Emit JSON-lines envelopes for streaming to minimize parser state in clients; downside: small bandwidth overhead per-line.
Default soft-fail loop policy allows fallback to compatible variant to avoid hard failures for customers with mixed adapter fleets.
Compatibility heuristics may produce false positives; we add confidence metadata so consumers can decide how to treat heuristically-extracted content.
implementation_notes: - Add executor envelope generator at runtime/core/executor/orbit_envelope.go - Implement LRU fingerprint cache with configurable capacity per-request in runtime/core/executor/fingerprint.go - Add compatibility shim package under internal/adapters/orbit_shims - Update streaming protocol to nl-delimited JSON lines; backward compatibility toggled by feature-flag - Add integration test harness in infra/tests/orbit_integration_test.py
